newsitem.title: CANADA: WCE canola ends higher on commercial, local buying.
newsitem.headline: WCE canola ends higher on commercial, local buying.

text.p: WCE canola closed higher boosted by late commercial and local buying sparked partly by gains in CBOT soybean oil, floor sources said.
There was little sign of any exporter buying, however, with no overnight business reported as the Canadian dollar continued to strengthen.
Dealers also noted that the pace of farmer selling had slowed and hedge-selling sales were unlikely to pick up for several weeks with February traditionally a slow month.
"Not too much canola moves when it is 35 to 40 (degrees Celsius) below (freezing)," one WCE oilseed trader said.

Flaxseed closed lower with light-hedge-related selling noted while potential buyer backed away from the market amid sentiment that Canadian supplies appear overpriced relative to competitive oils. March flax closed off $1.40 at $352.50.
Feed wheat closed higher aided by commission house buying on March which finished $0.90 higher at $170.50.

Western barley ended slightly lower although scale-down commercial buying interest was noted. February closed down $0.40 at $138.60. December feed peas ended down US$0.50 at US$186.00. Oats remained tradeless.
(All values in Canadian dollars/tonne except peas, oats)
